chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Qur'an came down as four fourths: a quarter concerning us, a quarter concerning our enemies, a quarter is Sunan (Precedents) and Amthal (Similitudes), and a quarter is Faraid (Obligations) and Ahkam (Rulings).
ai.seo_question: How is the Quran divided into four parts according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) elucidates a four-fold division of the Qur'an, categorizing its revelation into sections concerning the Ahl al-Bayt, their adversaries, narrative parables (Sunan wa Amthal), and legal injunctions. This classification highlights the comprehensive nature of the Qur'an, balancing theological identity with practical jurisprudence and moral instruction. It underscores the Shia perspective that the Qur'an is not merely a book of law but a holistic guide encompassing historical precedent and esoteric guidance.

en.ammaar-muslim: [1562/1] al-Kafi: Abu Ali al-Ash’ari from Muhammad b. Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ishaq b. Ammar from Abi Basir from Abi Ja’far عليه السلام who said:

The Qur’an came down as four fourths: A quarter concerning us, a quarter concerning our enemies, a quarter is Sunan (Precedents) and Amthāl (Similitudes), and a quarter is Farāʾiḍ (Obligations) and Aḥkām (Rulings)
